newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps may cut Central Power & Light.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps may cut Central Power & Light.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Wednesday it has placed its credit ratings on Central Power & Light Co under review for a possible downgrade.
Central Power & Light is a unit of Central and South West Corp.
Duff & Phelps said about $1.8 billion in securities is affected.
Duff & Phelps said the action is a result of the "negative outcome" of the company's rate case.

On Tuesday the company said the Public Utility Commission of Texas ordered it cut base rates by about $30 million from the level existing prior to Central Power & Light's higher rates in May 1996. The commission also voted to require the company to lower its rates by an additional $16 million in both 1998 and 1999.
"The order will likely result in a customer refund of approximately $100 million and will pressure credit protection measures," Duff & Phelps said in a statement.

Duff & Phelps currently rates Central Power & Light's first mortgage bonds and collateralized pollution control revenue bonds (PCRBs) as Single-A, non-collateralized PCRBs as Single-A-Minus and preferred stock as Triple-B-Plus.

Central Power & Light will remain on "rating watch-down" pending the company's expected plea for a rehearing, which is expected to take at least 45 days and a complete review of management's strategy to mitigate the effects of the rate reduction, Duff & Phelps said.
